data.title: Paid Promotion Used to Microtarget Staff and Customers
data.summary:
Campaign content was promoted through paid advertising narrowly targeted at the
organisation's own staff, customers or local community, placing it in front of the
people whose opinion matters most while remaining invisible to everyone else.
data.description:
Paid targeting changes the economics of an influence operation. A few hundred units of
currency puts a claim in front of exactly the audience that can act on it, and because
delivery is selective the organisation frequently learns of it only when someone
screenshots an advertisement it cannot otherwise see.

This invisibility is the operational problem. Monitoring that relies on public search
will not find targeted advertising, and the organisation cannot rebut what it cannot
observe. Platform advertisement libraries are the only reliable route, and their
coverage differs sharply by platform and jurisdiction.

Record the advertiser identity exactly as the platform presents it, including any
disclosed payer. That identity is often the strongest attribution evidence in the whole
campaign, because payment leaves a record that posting does not.
data.recommendation:
* Search the advertisement libraries of each relevant platform for the organisation's own
  name, brands and executives, and do so on a schedule rather than on report.
* Report targeted advertisements to the platform under its advertising policy, which is
  usually enforced more strictly than its content policy.
* Ask staff and customers to forward promoted content they are shown; selective delivery
  makes them the only reliable sensors.
data.short_recommendation: Monitor platform ad libraries and report under advertising policy.
